module_name: Sentiment and Emotion Analysis: Lexicon, Classical ML, Transformers, ABSA, Multilingual
module_description: Module 9 escalates to supervised sentiment and emotion analysis: from lexicon and TF-IDF+SVC baselines to fine-tuned BERT/RoBERTa, plus multilingual models (XLM-R, mBERT) for cross-lingual transfer, aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) for brands/products, emotion taxonomies (GoEmotions, Ekman), and the hard cases - sarcasm, negation, mixed sentiment. Evaluation under class imbalance is treated seriously.
learning_outcomes: C3 Fine-tune a transformer for sentiment on an Indonesian corpus
C4 Apply ABSA to product/brand aspects
C5 Evaluate a sentiment model fairly under imbalance and report per-class metrics
methods_models: Fine-tuning (Hugging Face Trainer), class weighting/resampling, cross-validation, per-class metrics, calibration
Human validation sample for model labels
evaluation_metrics: Accuracy, macro-F1, balanced accuracy, Cohen's kappa vs human coders, calibration (Brier), per-class precision/recall
pitfalls_limitations: Aggregation of per-post sentiment to brand-level claims; sarcasm errors; translation artifacts; generalizing across topics and time
tools_stack: transformers, datasets, evaluate, scikit-learn, accelerate; Indonesian checkpoints (IndoBERT/IndoRoBERTa, NusaBERT)
commercial_platforms: Optional: commercial sentiment dashboards for benchmark comparison
tools_access_cost: Training can be done on free Colab/Kaggle GPUs; commercial platforms demoed read-only
lab_activities: Fine-tune IndoBERT on an Indonesian sentiment dataset; run ABSA on brand-tagged sentences; compare with an LLM zero-shot call
datasets_apis: Indonesian sentiment corpus (SmSA/SMSSA), English GoEmotions for emotion, product review corpus for ABSA
assessment_methods: Lab notebook submission plus a 1-page interpretation with error analysis; graded on correctness, interpretation and documentation
data_collection_workflow: Collect posts -> clean text -> build annotation/codebook (human + LLM) -> validate with kappa -> train/evaluate -> archive labelled data and prompts
textbooks: Jurafsky & Martin, Speech and Language Processing, ch. 6 and sentiment chapters
Silge & Robinson, Text Mining with R, ch. 8 (sentiment)
key_papers: Gilardi et al. (2023/2024) LLMs outperform expert and crowd coders - and its critiques
Tornberg (2024) best practices for text annotation with LLMs
Comparisons of NusaBERT/IndoBERT for Indonesian sentiment (2024-2026)
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: LLM zero-shot annotation is benchmarked against fine-tuned models; the curriculum teaches a bake-off with human validation rather than a single winner
industry_relevance: Core competency for social-listening analyst, insights researcher and content-strategy roles; employers (Pulsar, Talkwalker, Meltwater, Brandwatch) list sentiment/topic extraction as the default screening task for junior analysts.
localization_context: Indonesia-specific models and lexicons (IndoBERT family, NusaBERT, InSet) plus local datasets (Indonesian sentiment/emotion/hoax sets) are used as the primary lab material, because English-oriented models underperform on code-mixed colloquial Indonesian.
ethics_regulation: Annotation labor and consent, model reporting of error rates, and disclosure that automated affective labels on individuals can misrepresent them; UU PDP applies when the corpus contains identifiable user text.
case_study_scenarios: Measure sentiment of an Indonesian brand campaign across X and TikTok, including per-aspect breakdown.
